packet: docs/packets/M15/plan-n.md, Task N1 (design note docs/design/multi-camera.md, owner decision 6.4: three cameras, as in MAD)
derivation: Carried over unchanged from so101_pick_place.xml: every element and attribute -- the bodies, geoms, joints, inertials, actuators, <option>, <compiler>, <default> and the `overhead` camera. Only XML comments differ, and two <camera> elements are added. crates/es/tests/views.rs::the_views_scene_is_the_demo_scene_plus_two_cameras proves it: with the two cameras removed the parsed scene hashes to so101_pick_place.xml's scene_hash, which covers every entity (spec 5.3), and the overhead camera keeps its StableId.

Added `wrist` inside `camera_mount`: pos="0.0 0.055 -0.045" euler="-0.57 0 0", upstream menagerie's own `wrist_cam` pose, which so101_pick_place.xml removed because the demo then had one camera. Upstream's `mode="fixed"`, `resolution`, `sensorsize` and `focal` are not represented by SceneDesc and are not carried (as for the parent derivation). `fovy="70"` is chosen here: upstream's 3.6 mm lens on a 5.76 x 3.24 mm sensor spans about 77 x 48.5 degrees, and a square 96x96 frame at 70 degrees keeps the fixed jaw, the cube below the demonstration's approach waypoint and the bin's rim in view. The camera sits 4 mm clear of the mount's `camera_box2` plate on the side it faces away from.

Added `side`, fixed to the world: pos="0.18 0.40 0.26" xyaxes="-1 0 0 0 -0.447 0.894" fovy="45". It looks along -Y and 26.6 degrees down, at about (0.18, -0.04, 0.04), so the cube's whole draw (x 0.21-0.27, y -0.03-0.05, z 0.02) and the bin (interior x 0.09-0.19, y -0.15 to -0.05) are in the frame with the arm; image-right is world -X. It complements the top-down `overhead` camera with heights: the lift, the carry and the drop into the bin.
A camera carries no dynamics: crates/es-physics-backend/src/mjcf_out.rs does not emit cameras, so MuJoCo simulates this scene as it simulates so101_pick_place.xml.
measured: crates/es/tests/views.rs::render::the_cameras_see_the_cube_and_the_wrist_moves_with_the_gripper renders each camera with the CPU reference at 96x96 at five pinned cube positions (the draw's four corners and (0.24, 0.01)) and counts cube-coloured pixels, floor 16: `side` at the Task IR's reset pose 66-107; `wrist` at the approach waypoint (tool 45 mm above the cube, pitch -85 deg) 448-470. At the reset pose the wrist camera looks at the horizon (0 at every position) and the outstretched arm hides most of the draw from `overhead` (0, 21, 3, 29, 0); at the approach waypoint the gripper hides the cube from `overhead` (0 at every position).
